answer: A Sybil defense is identity staking with slashing: an agent locks a bond before it may register, vote, or claim work, and forfeits it once evidence ties many personas to one operator. Free identities make Sybils cheap, so staking prices each extra identity at the full stake plus hosting and key custody, and one shared withdrawal trail endangers the cluster. A thousand fakes then need a thousand stakes at risk, so attacker cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once. Bonds in an onyx-hard ledger cannot be double-pledged, and ferrous proof of shared timing can burn the ivory reserve.
